analysis: Market context: broad indices have bounced sharply from April lows but remain well below 52-week highs; many quality names are in early basing patterns at 13-40% of their 52-week range — classic Stage 1→2 transition territory. Portfolio is almost entirely cash ($100K), so this is the ideal moment to deploy deliberately into 3 concentrated, high-conviction setups rather than forcing entries. Selected PYPL (cheap fintech with strong FCF at 30% of range, confirmed uptrend), FTNT (cybersecurity compounder already above SMA200 — the only candidate on the list with that distinction — at 35% of range), and MSFT (highest-quality business on the list, flattening SMA50 slope, 32% of range). All three use 2x ATR stops, each positions risk ~1.35-1.5% of equity, total capital deployed ~73%, keeping ~27% in cash as a buffer. NNDM (1 share, +11%) is an immaterial position — leave it as-is. Avoided: HUM (+23.6% above SMA50 — extended), ADBE (SMA50 slope -5.4%, still falling knife), KKR (+9.8% above SMA50 in a mixed trend — too extended off recent bounce), COIN (-27.6% vs SMA200 with -22.2% revenue growth — not quality basing).

trades.entry_strategy: Limit order at $50.44 or better; if market pulls back to the $48-50 zone (near SMA50), that is an even better risk-adjusted entry. Do not chase above $53.
trades.rationale: FUNDAMENTAL: PayPal is absurdly cheap for its quality — forward P/E 8.71, PEG 0.91, ROE 25.7%, $3.3B FCF, $6.4B operating cash flow. The market is pricing in zero growth and permanent disruption, yet the business continues to generate enormous cash. New CEO Alex Chriss is rationalizing the portfolio and margin expansion is underway. TECHNICAL: Confirmed uptrend/basing at only 30% of 52-week range, +8% above SMA50 (not extended), SMA50 slope turning positive at +2.3%. This is classic Stage 1→2 transition: the downtrend has stopped and buyers are absorbing supply. Risk/reward is exceptional — a reversion to just the mid-range ($67) offers 6:1 reward vs 2x ATR risk.
trades.exit_plan: Exit on stop at $47.72 (2x ATR). Time stop: if price has not moved to $58+ within 90 days, re-evaluate thesis. Thesis break: if operating cash flow declines materially YoY, if CEO departure, or if new competitive evidence (Apple Pay, Block) suggests structural share loss. Consider trimming 1/3 at $62 to lock gains; let remainder ride toward 52w high for LTCG treatment if past 12-month mark.

trades.entry_strategy: Limit at $86 or slight pullback to $84-86 range (near SMA50). FTNT is the only candidate already above its SMA200 — do not wait for a deep pullback that may not come. Entry within 5% of SMA50 is ideal.
trades.rationale: FUNDAMENTAL: Fortinet is a cybersecurity compounder — ROE 135.7%, operating margin 32.8%, revenue growth 14.8%, FCF $1.7B. Its integrated ASIC-based platform has structural cost advantages over pure-software competitors. Enterprise firewall refresh cycle is accelerating as clients modernize network security for AI workloads. Reasonable forward P/E 26 for a business of this quality. TECHNICAL: The only screened candidate trading above its 200-day SMA (+3.8%), in a confirmed uptrend basing pattern at 35% of 52-week range. SMA50 slope is flattening/slightly positive. This is Weinstein Stage 2 with momentum confirmation — strongest technical setup on the list.
trades.exit_plan: Stop at $80.77 (2x ATR, below recent consolidation lows). Time stop: if no progress toward $95 within 60 days, reduce size. Thesis break: evidence of meaningful market share loss to Palo Alto or CrowdStrike, or if gross margins deteriorate significantly. Trim 1/3 at $100 near prior resistance; hold remainder for LTCG if thesis intact past 12 months.

trades.entry_strategy: Limit at $414 or mild pullback to $405-415 zone. Microsoft's SMA50 slope is flattening (-1.8%) after a sharp recovery from April lows — wait for further stabilization if the broader market weakens. Do not chase above $425.
trades.rationale: FUNDAMENTAL: Microsoft is the highest-quality business on the screened list by almost any measure — P/E 24.7x on $37B FCF, operating margin 46.3%, ROE 34%, revenue growth 18.3%, D/E only 30x. Azure cloud + Copilot AI monetization is just beginning to compound. This is a Buffett-style 'wonderful business at a fair price' — at 32% of its 52-week range, you are paying roughly the same multiple as 2019-2020 for a business that is structurally stronger. TECHNICAL: Mixed/sideways basing at 32% of range with a flattening SMA50 slope (-1.8% — was much more negative). Price is +4.6% above SMA50, which is not extended. The setup is early Stage 2, slightly less confirmed than FTNT but the quality premium justifies inclusion.
trades.exit_plan: Stop at $389.58 (2x ATR, below April 2025 lows). Time stop: if SMA50 does not begin a positive slope within 45 days, reduce to half-size. Thesis break: Azure growth decelerates below 25% QoQ, meaningful AI revenue miss, or antitrust action that structurally limits Office/Teams bundling. Ideal hold is past 12-month mark for LTCG treatment given the quality of the business.
